### Fighting Selfishness (Luke 22:24) - Your Daily Bible Verse - August 2
Author: Betsy St. Amant Haddox
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/your-daily-bible-verse/your-daily-bible-verse-august-2.html
Passage: Luke 22:24
Points:
- Selfishness is rooted in human nature and remains an ongoing struggle even after salvation.
- The disciples fell into arguing over personal greatness during their final Passover meal with Jesus.
- Craving recognition and putting our personal agendas first damages relationships and disrupts fellowship with God.
- Through the Holy Spirit, believers have the divine power to resist and defeat selfish desires.
- In God's upside-down kingdom, true greatness is found in humbly serving others.

### Who Is the Greatest?
Author: Jon Bloom
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/who-is-the-greatest
Passage: Luke 22:25-26
Points:
- Selfish ambition corrupts motives and can surface even during the most sacred moments.
- The disciples absurdly debated their own prominence right after Jesus instituted the Lord's Supper and warned of His betrayal.
- Instead of condemning their pride, Jesus graciously redirected their attention to His model of humble service.
- Comparing ourselves to others leads to deeper sin, whereas fixing our eyes on Jesus frees us from self-absorption.
- True satisfaction is found not in pursuing our own status, but in being captivated by Christ's glory.
